text:
Ivar Stenberg went second overall in June, one pick after Gavin McKenna, and a month and a half into his rookie season he's on San Jose's top line with Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith. That line put up eight points in Sunday's win over Nashville, and Stenberg had a goal and an assist. Through 23 games he has seven goals and 14 points, 0.61 a game, a touch ahead of the 0.56 median for forwards picked in the top four in their first full season.

Some context keeps it honest. Eight of his 14 points have come on the power play, and he's shooting 18.4%, well above where most rookies settle. At five-on-five the Sharks get only 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, so the even-strength game is still a work in progress, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has just six of his games so far, with no clear strength or weakness yet. His ice time is climbing (17:29 a night over his last ten). For a 19-year-old, it's a strong start; whether it holds at even strength is the thing to watch.
